series_key: developing a replay system — market simulation
mechanism: Before tick replay, LoadPrevBars injects prior M1 OHLC so indicators have history. Minimum M1 bars: n=(P×T)+T where P=largest indicator period and T=chart minutes (e.g. MA200 on M5 → 1005; max(P)=50 with T=30 → 1530). Ensures sensors are live at replay start.
data_needed: CSV of prior M1 bars (multi-day export); largest indicator period P; target TFs' minute counts.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: WIN$N / WINQ21 B3 mini-index; preview M1 bars 2021-08-03..05; ticks 2021-08-06; research on M5/M15/M30
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS an explicit warm-start sizing rule so any sensor stack is fully primed before live/replay observation begins.
quote: n = ( 200 * 5 ) + 5 … before the replay starts, you need to have at least 1005 1-minute bars in order to be able to build an average of 200.

series_key: developing a replay system — market simulation
mechanism: Daily M1 capacity ≈ ((F−K)×60)+M from session open/close hours (e.g. dollar futures 09:00–18:30 → 570 M1 bars; typical ~540). Days needed = warm-up bar count / avg daily bars; auctions shorten effective liquidity window so use averages.
data_needed: Asset session open/close (full hours + fractional minutes); warm-up bar target from prior formula.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: B3 futures vs equities session windows; dollar futures example; M1 base
why_new_for_mis: Converts indicator lookback into calendar days of history MIS must retain per instrument session length—liquidity-calendar aware data planning.

series_key: developing a replay system — market simulation
mechanism: When building M1 from real ticks, Event_OnTime accumulates volume_real (lots traded) into Rate.real_volume; tick_volume stays 0 until later because real ticks report traded size not move-count. Article stresses real_volume = how much traded vs tick_volume = how many moves.
data_needed: Tick CSV with last, volume_real, time_msc; custom symbol rates.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: B3 tick replay (WINQ21); M1 bars on custom symbol
why_new_for_mis: Separates traded-size liquidity from tick-count activity—MIS can avoid conflating the two when sensing participation.
quote: the real volume shows how many trades actually happened, while the tick volume shows how many moves happened.

series_key: developing a replay system — market simulation
mechanism: Corporate events (earnings, splits/grouping, futures expiry, bond issuance) adjust prices so stored M1 bars diverge from contemporaneous traded ticks; market reacts to the tick-perceived price, not the adjusted bar. Prefer archived traded ticks as ground truth; optional [TICKS->BARS] stage rebuilds preview M1 from ticks then strips ticks from replay buffer.
data_needed: Daily archived tick CSVs; optional M1 bar CSVs; config stages [BARS]/[TICKS]/[TICKS->BARS].
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: WIN$N M1 preview days + WINQ21 ticks (Aug 2021 examples); any asset with corporate actions
why_new_for_mis: Explicit data-integrity sensing rule: when bars and ticks disagree after corporate events, trust ticks—MIS should flag bar/tick inconsistency as a regime/data-change event.
quote: Once information is lost, it is impossible to get it back… the bar data may not coincide with the values of the traded ticks.

series_key: developing a replay system — market simulation
mechanism: [BARS->TICKS] + PointsPerTick config: SimuleBarToTicks walks open→low, low→high, high→close via Pivot; each leg inserts 0.382 then 0.618 Fibonacci waypoints snapped to tick size, then endpoint; volume split evenly across simulated tickets; timestamps spread across ~60s. Produces ~1-minute real-time path for manual stress practice (not Strategy Tester).
data_needed: M1 OHLC+real_volume CSV; POINTSPERTICK (e.g. 5 for index futures); [CONFIG]/[BARS->TICKS] sections.

series_key: developing a replay system — market simulation
mechanism: Real tape can jump 3 ticks with no prints (liquidity hole) then fall 1; OHLC simulation still walks every tick step between open/high/low/close. Article shows real vs simulated path diagrams—modeling fills gaps that never traded. Min useful tickets ≥3 (open/extreme/close). Four OHLC topologies cover all bar shapes.
data_needed: True tick tape for comparison; M1 OHLC; tick size.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Generic M1 bar simulation; stock tick=0.01, dollar futures=0.5, index futures=5 points
why_new_for_mis: Frames missing intermediate ticks as a liquidity-hole signature MIS can detect by comparing sparse real prints to dense OHLC-implied paths.
